data.title: BioID-screening identifies PEAK1 and SHP2 as components of the Alk “proximitome” in neuroblastoma cells
data.projectDescription: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) is a receptor tyrosine kinase (RTK) that is mutated in approximately 10% of pediatric cancer neuroblastoma (NB). To shed light on ALK-driven signaling processes, we employed BioID-based in vivo proximity labeling to identify molecules that interact with ALK. NB cells expressing inducible ALK-BirA* fusion proteins were generated and stimulated with ALKAL ligands in the presence and absence of the ALK tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) lorlatinib. LC/MS-MS analysis identified multiple proteins, including PEAK1 and SHP2, which were validated as ALK interactors in NB cells. Further analysis of the ALK-SHP2 interaction confirmed that the ALK-SHP2 interaction as well as SHP2-Y542 phosphorylation was dependent on ALK activation. Use of the SHP2 inhibitors, SHP099 and RMC-4550, resulted in inhibition of cell growth in ALK-driven NB cells. In addition, we noted a strong synergistic effect of combined ALK and SHP2 inhibition that was specific to ALK-driven NB cells, suggesting a potential therapeutic option for ALK-driven NB.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Streptavidin beads with bound proteins were washed twice with 1 ml 50 mM TEAB (triethylammonium bicarbonate) and digested with 0.5 µg LysC Mass Spec grade (Promega) in 100 µl 50 mM TEAB at 37 °C for 3h while flipping the tubes every 30 min. Samples were reduced in 5 mM TCEP for 30 min at room temperature and alkylated in 10 mM MMTS for 30 min at room temperature. A second digestion was performed with 0.3 µg Pierce MS grade Trypsin (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 37°C and incubated overnight. Next morning the digested samples were removed from beads with a magnetic stand and the beads washed twice with 50 µl 50 mM TEAB which was pooled with the supernatants. Digested peptides were labelled using Tandem Mass Tag reagents, TMTpro 16-plex (Thermo Scientific) according to the manufacturer instructions. The combined set was fractionated to 5 fractions using Pierce High pH Reversed-Phase Peptide Fractionation Kit (Thermo Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The fractions were dried in a vacuum centrifuge and reconstituted in 15 μl of 3% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid for analysis. Fractions were analyzed on an Orbitrap Fusion™ Lumos™ Tribrid™ mass spectrometer interfaced with Easy-nLC1200 liquid chromatography system (Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were trapped on an Acclaim Pepmap 100 C18 trap column (100 μm x 2 cm, particle size 5 μm, Thermo Fischer Scientific) and separated on an in-house packed analytical column i.d. 75 μm, particle size 3 μm, Reprosil-Pur C18, Dr. Maisch, length 35 cm  using a linear gradient from 5% to 33% B over 77 min followed by an increase to 100% B for 3 min, and 100% B for 10 min at a flow of 300 nL/min. Solvent A was 0.2% formic acid and solvent B was 80% acetonitrile, 0.2% formic acid. Precursor ion mass spectra were acquired at 120 000 resolution and a scan range of 375-1500 m/z. The most abundant ions with a charge state of 2-7 were picked for data-dependent MS/MS analysis. The MS/MS analysis was performed using a “top speed” duty cycle of 3 s, collision induced dissociation (CID) collision energy 30%, isolation window 0.7 m/z, maximum injection time 60 ms. Dynamic exclusion was set to 45 s and mass tolerance to 10 ppm. The top 10 MS/MS fragment ions were isolated via simultaneous multinotch isolation within an m/z range of 400-1400 for MS3 fragmentation using higher-energy collision dissociation (HCD) collision energy 55%, m/z range 100-500 and a maximum injection time of 120 ms. The MS3 spectra for reporter ion quantitation were recorded with a resolution of 50 000.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: The data files were merged for identification and relative quantification using Proteome Discoverer version 2.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The data was matched against the Swissprot homo sapiens database using Mascot version 2.5.1 (Matrix Science) as a search engine. The precursor mass tolerance was set to 5 ppm and fragment mass tolerance to 0.6 Da. Tryptic peptides were accepted with one missed cleavage, variable modifications of methionine oxidation and fixed cysteine alkylation, TMT-label modifications of N-terminus and lysine were selected. TMT reporter ions were identified in the MS3 HCD spectra with 3 mmu mass tolerance. Percolator was used for the validation of identified proteins. The data was filtered for medium (<5%) and high (<1%) protein FDR.
